info.title: Rust proc-macro crate for source parsing

diffs.patch:
Index: Cargo.toml
===================================================================
--- Cargo.toml	
+++ Cargo.toml	
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+[package]
+name = "syn-transform"
+version = "0.1.0"
+edition = "2021"
+description = "A procedural-macro crate that parses Rust source into a syntax tree it can inspect and transform"
+license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
+
+[lib]
+proc-macro = true
+
+[dependencies]
+proc-macro2 = "1"
+quote = "1"
+syn = { version = "2", features = ["full", "extra-traits", "fold", "visit-mut"] }

parts.text:
No crt1.o / Scrt1.o. So linking standard binaries is not feasible. We cannot run build scripts.

Alternative: verify our crate's syntax without compiling dependencies by using `rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type proc-macro` with `--emit=metadata`? That still requires dependencies (syn, quote) which must be compiled, and their build scripts need running. But if we could get vendored precompiled? No.

Alternative verification: use `rustc` to parse our lib.rs only for syntax errors: `rustc -Zparse-only` is nightly. We have stable. But we can do `rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type proc-macro src/lib.rs --emit=metadata --extern syn=...` impossible without syn.

However, cargo check with the pure-Rust fallback? The build failures are only due to build scripts needing a linker. Could we get around linking build scripts by using `-C linker=rust-lld` plus providing libc? Not enough.

Maybe there's a musl target and a static linker? Still needs crt.

Alternative: Install a linker without root. We could download prebuilt Zig (which bundles a linker and libc for cross-compilation!) and use `zig cc` as linker. Zig cc can compile/link C and Rust can use it. But architecture aarch64 host. Zig supports aarch64-linux. Zig cc can provide libc (it ships musl/glibc?). Zig bundles its own libc headers and can link against system glibc for native target. This could work: set CC=zig cc and linker=zig cc. But downloading Zig (~50MB) may be acceptable.

Even simpler: Does Zig provide crt files? Zig bundles musl and can produce static binaries without system crt. For native glibc target it uses system glibc but Zig includes some crt? Zig's `zig cc` for native linux-gnu can link using system libc if present; but crt1.o missing on system—Zig provides its own `crt1.o` for glibc? Zig ships `libc` stubs for many targets including glibc start files. I think Zig can link a native binary using its bundled glibc or its own.

Alternatively use target `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` which is statically linked by Zig and doesn't need system libc. But that requires adding the musl target via rustup (needs network, fine) and self-contained musl crt comes from rust's `self-contained`? Rust's musl target uses `self-contained` musl libc initially but for aarch64-unknown-linux-musl it needs a musl linker (`musl-gcc`) normally. With Zig as linker it works.

This is getting heavy. Let me weigh: The task is to set up the crate. Verification is desirable but optional. Installing Zig and musl target to run tests is a lot. But I can at least verify the library compiles by getting dependencies compiled. Build scripts for proc-macro2/quote/unicode-ident need linking.
